Back in 2007, when we launched Gardasil in the UK, we saw first-hand that you only drive uptake in sensitive areas (HPV, sex, stigma) when you really understand local culture, language and unspoken fears. That’s why I love this work Laurie Morgan 's sharing from Sure / Rexona: brilliant use of a very British “fear of body odour” insight, built on solid Marketing Fundamentals with a modern “+”. Different category, same truth: if you want to change behaviour, you have to be brave enough to talk about what people are actually worried about. #Oxfordsm #behaviourchange #marketing ...more

You adopted AI. But did anything actually change? I've seen this pattern play out dozens of times now. Companies buy the tools. Run the pilots. Build a few agents. Celebrate the progress. Then they stop. Here's why: → The org chart looks identical to 2023 → Approval chains haven't moved → Workflows are untouched → AI is bolted on top of the old operating model And then leaders wonder why the ROI isn't showing up. The tools are not the bottleneck. The structure underneath is. Here's what the 6% did differently: → They started measuring outcomes. → They changed how decisions get made →They rebuilt how humans and AI work together → They redesigned workflows before deploying AI The gap between "experimenting" and "transforming" isn't more tools. It's the willingness to change how work actually flows. The jump is hard. But staying on the wrong side is harder. 👉 Follow Jonny Tooze for more on AI-native transformation. ♻️ Repost if someone in your network needs to see this.

To my American friends trying to reach their French business contacts in May: You are not being ghosted. You have simply entered "Les Ponts". 😱 In France, May is not a month. It is a strategic obstacle course of public holidays, long weekends, and calendar-based escape artistry. “Faire le pont” literally means “to make the bridge.” In practice, it means that when a public holiday falls on a Tuesday or Thursday, many people take the Monday or Friday off too, creating a beautiful long weekend. What are they doing with this time? Maybe Djing ! 😎

We're hearing about three #meningitis cases this evening (Thursday 14th May), this time near #Reading in Berkshire. Sadly, one death has been reported, with two other youngsters being treated. The thoughts of all us at Meningitis Now are with the families and friends of those young people tonight. My message this evening for people to remain vigilant and aware of the signs and symptoms of the disease. Meningitis can become life-threatening very quickly and early treatment can be critical. Symptoms can appear in any order and may include a high temperature, severe headache, vomiting, stiff neck, sensitivity to light, confusion, drowsiness, cold hands and feet, severe muscle pain, and a rash that does not fade under pressure. It is important to remember that not everyone will experience all symptoms. This situation is a tragic reminder of why Meningitis Now 's “No Plan B for MenB” campaign is calling for greater protection for young people. MenB is one of the most common causes of bacterial meningitis in the UK. Its impact is devastating, yet preventable. Since 2015, only infants have been vaccinated against #MenB , but we believe all teenagers and young adults should be protected by this vaccine on the #NHS . The MenB vaccine is not available to teenagers and young adults on the NHS routine immunisation schedule, but we believe it should be. Currently, it is only available for this age group privately through high street and supermarket pharmacies. You can find out more at www.meningitisnow.org or call our nurse-led Helpline on 0808 80 10 388. #meningitis , #vaccines , UK Health Security Agency , #NHS

What's the superpower of great design? It's turning something useful to something so irresistible that users can't but adopt it, stick to it and love it. Health related behaviors may well be the most defining changes in people's lives that positively impact one's life trajectories. Healthy behavior interventions deserve the best design to make them adopted, sticked to and loved. In our Population Health Strategy mission to accelerate what's possible in prevention of Type 1 Diabetes progression, I've been fortunate to work with the best Sanofi designers Sylvia Park-Ekecs Kanu Goel Sébastien Laurent Renard Jesse Alvarez Kristin Chand from Florent Edouard 's team, surrounded by fantastic colleagues Antoine Barbot , Zizhuo (April) Wu Monica Bertolini and Pien Klieverik . A vision of persons living with Type 1 Diabetes - members of the TH1NK AHEAD Think & Do Tank - turned in their minds and hands into a powerful concept designed to make the screening journey for Type 1 Diabetes easier: The Screening ALL1. Thank you iF Design for awarding our concept of preventative care ecosystem this year. It confirms, that starting with the lived experience of potential users is right - Nothing for them without them! It gave us a fantastic boost of energy (Photo 1 😉), it gave us space to promote early detection of Type 1 Diabetes outside healthcare space (Photo 2 💙), at it gives us all a good reason to implement this care intervention as new standard of care as soon as possible. Onwards! 🚀
